usage: jbus [-h] [--project PROJECT] [--as PARTY] [--evidence SOURCE:REF]
            {poll,alarm,status,events,digest,view,word,queue,plan,gate,answer,done,project,t3} ...

The one entry point: `jbus poll`, `jbus queue
show|add|approve|hold|remove|apply`, `jbus plan [close <entry>]`, `jbus gate
<slug>`, `jbus answer <number>`, `jbus done <slug>`, `jbus status`, `jbus
events`, `jbus digest`, `jbus alarm`, `jbus view`, `jbus word`, `jbus project
add`, and `jbus t3 login|launch-test`. `jbus poll` is one pass over every
project in the config, under one lock: it runs `jmerge` where the home is off,
reads what the threads wrote down, asks T3 Code and GitHub what is out, sends
a line for each finding, ties each crew to its thread (the link, the relay and
the settle), tells a crew whose pull request `jmerge` calls stale or
conflicting to rebase, and one whose pull request is short of something it can
fix what to do (`expedite`), launches the rows of the queue that were
approved, rewrites the table's derived columns (with why each row waits, and a
line for each change of status), says what waits on the user (`stall`), again
each hour, and rewrites the one list of it (`waiting`). A row that ended with
something left is sent to its home to close, once (`leftover`): it waits on
that home, and on the user only where it has no home or the home did not close
it. The launches come after every project was asked what is out: `max_running`
caps the crews out across all of them, and the free slots go to the projects
in turn (`rotation`). A gate a thread pipes to `jbus gate` is a question with
a number (`questions`): it waits on the user until `jbus answer` closes it,
and a pass carries an answer that is not the default to the thread that asked.
Everything it finds is an event with a loudness (`wake.LOUDNESS`), and the
project's home thread is woken only for what the user must act on: a new
question, a hold or an approval that is theirs, an alert, a stall. Everything
else is quiet: it is in the log, which `jbus events` prints and the view
shows. A failure that repeats is told once, and once when it ends (`alert`).
`jbus word` is the user's word down to a home: it keeps what the user said for
one project or for all, and sends it to the thread in each home's `home-id` as
a queued message, at once and then on each pass until it went (`word`). It is
no event, so it wakes nothing. Once a day it asks `jmerge` what a sweep would
remove, and again on each pass until `jmerge` has run. Each pass ends by
rewriting the status file, which `jbus status` prints: what a home thread that
is down cannot say. `jbus view` is no pass: it is a server that shows what the
passes left, and it reads no config (`jbus.view`). `jbus project add` is no
pass either: it adds one project's table to the config, and the next pass
loads it (`jbus.project`). A scratch home of the config is no project of the
pass, and no repo step is run for it (`jbus.load`): its words go to its thread
in a chore of the pass (`word.scratch`). Beside the status file is the record
of the pass (`record`), written when the pass starts and again when it ends.
No model reads anything.

positional arguments:
  {poll,alarm,status,events,digest,view,word,queue,plan,gate,answer,done,project,t3}
    poll                one pass over every project
    alarm               count a pass that did not finish: the third in a row
                        alerts
    status              what the last pass left: the status file and pass.json
    events              every event jbus sent, JSON lines
    digest              what waits and what moved, over every project
    view                serve the bus as a page, read-only
    word                the user's word to a project's home, or to every home
    queue               the queue table and the Chef's four verbs
    plan                each entry of the home's plan.md, its status counted
                        from its queue rows
    gate                keep a question for the user, its lines on stdin
    answer              close a question with the user's answer
    done                send a result now, its lines on stdin
    project             the projects of the config
    t3                  the sign-in to the T3 Code server, and one test launch

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --project PROJECT     the project's name in the config, when it has several
  --as PARTY            who acts in a go or an answer: home, the default, or
                        user, on the user's own words that jbus reads
                        (--message or --page); the bot acts only over POST
                        /act
  --evidence SOURCE:REF
                        the words a go or an answer rests on, as
                        <source>:<ref>, in place of its basis option:
                        t3-message, lavish-page, typed (a word's id) or answer
